title: Microbiome
summary: The microbiome is the community of trillions of tiny organisms - mostly bacteria - that live in and on our bodies. Explore where they live, the many helpful jobs they do, and why a balanced microbiome matters for health.

compareCandidate.label: Your microbiome vs. a microbial community
compareCandidate.description: The microbiome is one special case of a microbial community - the one living in and on you. Like an ecosystem, it is made of many species that interact, help, and balance one another.

plainLanguageExplanation: The microbiome is the community of trillions of tiny organisms - mostly bacteria, plus some fungi - that live in and on your body. The biggest collection lives in the gut (intestines). These microbes are not invaders; they are normally helpful. They help digest food, make some vitamins, train the immune system, and crowd out harmful germs. A balanced microbiome supports health, while an out-of-balance one has been linked to issues, which is why doctors care about it and why good habits like eating fiber and being careful with antibiotics help.

whyItMatters: Your body is home to an ecosystem of trillions of helpful microbes. Understanding the microbiome explains how food is digested, why some vitamins are made, and why a healthy diet and careful antibiotic use matter - and it shows how 'germs' are mostly our partners, not our enemies.
tagline: The tiny ecosystem that lives on and in you
didYouKnow: Your body carries roughly as many microbial cells as human cells - you are, in a sense, a walking ecosystem.
